topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the students to the final course session and outlines the learning objectives on cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional Modalities: Surgery, Radiotherapy, and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss traditional cancer treatment approaches, detailing their mechanisms of action, clinical successes, and toxicity limitations.

topics.label: Exploiting Intrinsic Cellular Vulnerabilities and Checkpoint Defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapeutic strategies that target intrinsic cancer cell vulnerabilities, including hormone receptor dependencies, cell cycle checkpoint failures, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Oncogene Addiction and Small Molecule Kinase Inhibitors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on treating cancers driven by hyperactivated kinases and examine the resulting challenges of cross-reactivity, drug resistance, and bypass pathways.

topics.label: Targeted Monoclonal Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates selectively bind cell-surface targets to disrupt oncogenic signaling or deliver cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Immunotherapy and T-Cell-Directed Therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe methods for harnessing the immune system against cancer, covering immune surveillance, checkpoint blockade, bispecific engagers, and CAR T-cell engineering.

topics.label: Broad Challenges, Historical Progress, and Future Directions in Oncology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize the broader systemic challenges, historical survival improvements, emerging technologies, and ethical considerations shaping modern cancer management.
